result.topic_en: Gauss argues that for the hypergeometric-type series with sum S = ((n+θ)(n+θ+1)...(n+θ+k-1))/((n+1)(n+2)...(n+k)), the remainder S − S_m of a partial sum always has the same sign as the first omitted term, and gives an easy proof for the case 1−θ positive using alternating terms that first increase and then decrease in absolute value.
